provenance: This is a layered-configuration store with a declared precedence order, plus a written conformance contract for how a resolver must behave. records.json holds one record per managed entity, each carrying a `layers` object whose keys are exactly the layer names declared in rules.json#/precedence (`user`, `environment`, `default`) and whose values are strings or null; rules.json is a policy document with `mode`, an identifying `key` field, and an ordered `precedence` array; output_contract.json is a normative spec fixing accepted input shape, rejection conditions, output row shape (`id`, `value`, `source`, `resolved`), key order, sort order, an empty-population reference result, and an execution envelope. That combination -- named layers, an ordered override chain, `null` meaning fall through while empty string is a real resolved value, a `source` field naming which layer won, and resolved/unresolved counters -- is the exact data model of a configuration-management or feature-flag platform: LaunchDarkly's ordered targeting rules with a default/fallthrough at the bottom, Azure App Configuration's key-values differentiated by label (`(No label)` being the base layer), Unleash's per-environment strategy stack, Spring Cloud Config's profile chain, AWS AppConfig's configuration profiles per environment. An operator producing this data would have had a config store's configuration explorer open on one side and the governance policy / precedence editor on the other, and would be reconciling them against a written standard -- the same posture as a release engineer auditing which environment's value actually wins in production. The FSM re-dresses that model as a transmission operator's SCADA setpoint-governance console (assets instead of keys, override layers instead of labels, an authority ladder instead of a rule stack, a commissioning standard instead of a schema doc), so the interface should read as an industrial config-governance console: config-platform structure and restraint, grid-operations vocabulary and units.
reference_products: LaunchDarkly (feature management / flag targeting -- the category leader, and the closest structural match to a precedence order). Contributed: (a) the Flags list as the model for a registry -- a big 24px page title with borderless icon+label dropdown triggers (Views / Filters / Sort / Display) right-aligned on the same line, exactly ONE filled indigo primary button at the end of that row, a full-width search field below it, then a single bordered white card containing the table; (b) the ordered rule stack -- each rule is its own white card and the cards are joined by a 1px vertical connector line with a small circular '+' between them, so ordering is a physically drawn ladder rather than a numbered list, with a 6-dot drag grip on the left of an editable rule; (c) sentence-form logic ('If **user plan type** is one of `Beta tester`' -- bold for field names, a grey chip for literal values, a blue-tinted chip for references), and 'Serve' rendered as a small grey label + a coloured diamond glyph + plain text rather than a badge; (d) variation-identity colour: each variation owns one colour (teal / amber) reused as an 8px diamond next to the flag name, as the fill of the rollout bar, and beside 'Serve' -- colour carries identity, never decoration; (e) environment columns headed by a small coloured dot + the environment name; (f) the filter popover, whose selected pills are outlined in indigo with indigo text and NO fill, with a small indigo count badge on the trigger.

Azure App Configuration, in the Azure portal (Configuration explorer). Contributed: the whole administrative chrome -- 'Home > store-name' breadcrumb, an icon + bold resource name + ' | Section name' title with a small grey resource-type subtitle beneath it, a left blade of grouped nav (an 'Operations' group and a 'Settings' group, each a small coloured glyph + 13px label, a search box pinned above them, active row a flat grey fill); a borderless command bar of icon+label text actions (+ Create, Refresh, Manage view, Collapse, Expand, Values, Edit, Delete) where unavailable actions are simply greyed rather than hidden and NOTHING in the bar is a filled button; light-blue removable filter pills reading 'Labels : Select label ✕'; a bare-text result count line ('Loaded 3 key-values with 3 unique keys.'); and a 32px-row grid with a checkbox column, sentence-case headers carrying an ↑↓ sort glyph, and a row-end '...' menu. Most importantly it contributed the sentinel convention this task lives or dies on: an absent or withheld cell is written as italic grey parenthesised text -- `(No label)`, `(Hidden value)` -- never left blank, and revision deltas are tiny outline glyphs in a 20px gutter column (green ⊞ added, amber ⊡ modified, red ⊟ removed) rather than tinted row backgrounds.

Unleash (open-source feature management). Contributed: the left navigation -- ~280px, white, flat 15px text with 20px line icons, one violet accent, active item a pale violet fill with a 3px accent bar on its left edge and rounded right corners, a nested 'Configure' group whose children swap the icon for a small filled accent square, and a 'Hide (⌘+B)' collapse control pinned to the bottom; a small accent-coloured breadcrumb link above a large page title with a tab strip under it (active tab a 3px accent underline); and the modal language -- a wide white sheet at ~16px radius over a dimmed canvas, a 26px title, a row of filter pills at the top, then grouped sections of selectable option cards (flat #F5F5F8 fill, no border, icon left, bold title over a two-line grey description; selected = pale accent fill).

AWS AppConfig and Spring Cloud Config were read for vocabulary only (configuration profile, environment, deployment strategy, profile chain, `application-{profile}.yml` overlay order) -- they confirmed that 'which layer supplied this value' is named as a *source* in real tools, and that the base layer is conventionally called `default` and shown last.

design_tokens.palette:
Two planes and one accent. Canvas #F6F7F9; every content surface is a plain white #FFFFFF card on it with a 1px #E4E6EB border, 10px radius and NO shadow. Inside a card, row separators are a lighter hairline #ECEEF1; table header rows take a #F7F8FA fill. Text: primary #14161A, secondary #5C636E, tertiary/placeholder/disabled #8A919C. Exactly one saturated accent, indigo #4F46E5 -- used for link text, the single filled primary button per screen, the 2px focus ring at 35% alpha, the active sidebar item (pale #EEF0FE fill + 3px #4F46E5 left bar), the outline of a selected filter pill (1.5px border + indigo label, no fill), the 3px active-tab underline, and a small circular count badge. Nothing else is indigo.

Layer identity is its own small palette, assigned per authority layer and reused unchanged wherever that layer appears (an 8px rotated-square diamond beside a layer name, the tick colour on the authority ladder, the left edge of a ledger row, the source cell in the resolved table): rank 1 teal #0E9AA7, rank 2 amber #D98C1F, rank 3 slate #64748B, and if a policy ever declares more layers, continue with violet #7C5CD6, rose #C2506B, moss #4E8C57. These are identity tokens, never severity.

Status colour appears only inside 20px pills and 8px glyphs, never as a filled row or a page banner: resolved #14663D text on #E4F4EA fill / #BFE3CD border; unresolved #5C636E on #F0F1F4 / #DEE1E6 (deliberately grey, not red -- an unresolved setpoint is a fact, not an error); rejected/non-conforming #A3221B on #FDECEA / #F3C8C3; pending #8A5A00 on #FDF4E3 / #EFDCB4.

Control-room chrome on the overview surface is the ONLY place additional colour is allowed, and even there it is thin: the advisory banner is a #FDF4E3 strip with a 1px #EFDCB4 border, a 16px amber glyph and #6B4A00 text -- full width, 40px, one line, no icon-in-a-circle; the alarm badge is a 8px #B3261E dot plus a count in #14161A, never a filled red block; frequency deviation and load-vs-forecast are large tabular-mono numbers in #14161A that switch to #A3221B only when outside band; the generation-mix figure is a single 8px stacked horizontal bar using the layer-identity ramp, no legend colours invented beyond it. No gradients, no coloured page headers, no dark mode, no hero imagery.
design_tokens.typography:
UI face: system stack -- -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Inter, Roboto, sans-serif. Page title 24px/600/-0.01em; section heading 16px/600; card/panel title 15px/600; row primary (an asset identifier in a list) 15px/600; body and table cells 13.5px/400; form labels 13px/500; secondary metadata and captions 12.5px/400 in #5C636E; helper/footnote 12px/400 in #8A919C. Column headers are 13px/500 sentence case in #14161A -- NOT 10px uppercase micro-caps; that habit belongs to CMS admin panels, and neither reference product uses it. Line-height 1.5 for prose, 1.35 inside tables, 1.7 for the standard's clause body.

Mono face: ui-monospace, 'JetBrains Mono', 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace, 12.5px, and it carries real semantic weight -- it marks a value that is data rather than prose. In mono: asset identifiers, authority layer names, every stored layer value, resolved values and source names, policy mode and key field, revision numbers, kV / MW / MVA / Hz readings, counts in the counter row, and the whole reference-annex payload. In the UI face: page titles, section headings, human names, committee names, districts, notes, and every sentence of the standard's clause text. Numeric table columns use tabular-nums and right alignment. Italic is reserved for exactly one thing: parenthesised sentinel text for a value that does not exist (see components). No small-caps, no letter-spacing tricks outside the -0.01em on the page title.
design_tokens.density: Administrative-dense, not cramped. The registry table uses a two-line row at 56px (identifier line + operational metadata line, 14px horizontal cell padding) so ~11 rows sit above the fold at 900px; the override ledger and the resolved-rows table use a single-line 34px row with 12px padding so 20+ rows read at once. Header rows 36px. Sidebar item 34px. Buttons 32px (28px for a compact toolbar action). Inputs 34px, search field 40px. Filter pill 30px. Status pill 20px. Card padding 16px, 20px for a document-reader panel. Page gutter 24px, content max-width 1280px then centred. 20px between the page header and the first card; 28px above a new section heading; 12px between stacked form fields. Definition-grid rows (label left / value right) 30px with an 8px gap. Clause paragraphs get 12px of separation and a 68ch measure.
design_tokens.components:
TABLE -- one white card per table, hairline #ECEEF1 rule under each row, a #F7F8FA header row, NO vertical rules, NO zebra striping, hover tints the row #FAFBFC. Sortable headers show a small ↑↓ glyph that is grey when inactive and #14161A when the column is the active sort. Optional 20px leading gutter column carrying an 8px layer-identity diamond or a delta glyph. A row-end '...' icon button opens a menu of icon+label items. Row count is a bare 12.5px grey sentence above the card ('124 assets in this region', '6 rows'), never a badge.

ABSENCE SENTINELS (the single most important component here) -- three conditions must stay visually distinct without inference, following the Azure convention: a layer the record does not declare renders as italic #8A919C `(not declared)` in the UI face; a declared layer holding null renders as italic #8A919C `(no value)` with the layer's identity diamond still shown at full strength, because the layer IS present; a declared layer holding a zero-length string renders as mono `""` in #14161A inside a 2px-padded #F0F1F4 chip with the caption `empty string` in 12px #5C636E beneath or beside it. Never collapse any two into a blank cell, an em dash, or the word 'none'.

AUTHORITY LADDER -- the ordering figure, taken from LaunchDarkly's rule stack: a vertical column of white cards, one per layer, joined by a 1px #DEE1E6 connector line running through a 24px gap between them; each card shows a 22px circular rank chip (near-black #14161A fill, white 12px/600 number) on the left, the layer name in mono 14px, its identity diamond, and a 12.5px grey qualifier ('highest authority' on rank 1, 'base layer' on the last). Ranks are printed, not implied by position alone.

PILLS AND CHIPS -- status pill: 20px, 4px radius, 12px/600, tinted fill + 1px tinted border, optional 6px leading glyph; value chip: #F0F1F4 fill, no border, 4px radius, mono 12.5px; reference chip (links to another surface): #EEF0FE fill, #4F46E5 text; removable filter pill: 30px, pill radius, #EEF3FF fill, 13px text reading 'Region : North ✕'. Filter-popover selection pills are the outlined kind -- white with a 1px #E0E2E7 border, and when selected a 1.5px #4F46E5 border with #4F46E5 text and still no fill.

BUTTONS -- 6px radius. Primary: solid #4F46E5, white 13.5px/500, at most one per screen and always the rightmost action. Secondary: white with a 1px #D9DCE1 border, #14161A text. Toolbar dropdown trigger: borderless, 13.5px/500 near-black, 16px line icon on the left and a chevron on the right, no background until hover (#F0F1F4). Tertiary: borderless #4F46E5 text. Destructive is text-only in #A3221B. Icon-only buttons are 32px, borderless, 16px stroke icons.

DISCLOSURE -- a collapsed section is a full-width 44px row inside the card: a 16px chevron, a 15px/600 title, and a 12.5px grey summary that states only that content exists ('Override ledger', 'not yet opened') and never leaks a count or a layer name. Expanding animates height only and reveals the ledger table in place; the chevron rotates. Same component serves the standard's three parts.

DEFINITION GRID -- for policy and asset attributes: a two-column grid, 13px/500 #5C636E label on the left at a fixed 180px, mono or UI-face value on the right, one 30px row each, separated by #ECEEF1 hairlines, inside a plain white card. This is how the governing mode, key field, effective date, approving committee, review cadence, nameplate rating, feeder and voltage class are presented.

DOCUMENT READER -- the commissioning standard renders as a reading panel, not a form: a white card at 20px padding, a 68ch measure, clause numbers ('4.2') in mono 12.5px #8A919C hanging in a 48px left gutter, clause titles 15px/600, body 13.5px/400 at 1.7, and any normative literal (a field name, a type, an error class, a key order) set in mono inside a #F0F1F4 chip so specification text and specification values never blur. A right-hand 200px 'On this part' anchor list of clause titles, plain text with the active one in #4F46E5.

RENDERED DOCUMENT / EXPORT -- the conformance matrix opens as a paper-like surface: white, 8px radius, a hairline border, 32px padding, a document header block (title, revision, generated timestamp, count of rows) above a 1px #DEE1E6 rule, then a plain numbered table of checks with a 40px '#' column. It carries a 'Download' secondary button and a monospaced filename caption. No app chrome inside it.

POPOVER / MODAL -- popovers and dropdowns are the only elements with a shadow (0 6px 20px rgba(16,24,40,.10)), 10px radius, 1px #E4E6EB border. The filter popover is 320px with a 22px title + ✕, hairline-separated sections, and a right-aligned outline 'Clear' in the footer. Modals are 12px radius over a rgba(20,22,26,.40) scrim and are reserved for the export dialog and destructive confirmations.

PAGINATION -- a bare row under the card: '1-25 of 124' in 12.5px #5C636E on the left, and on the right numbered page buttons as 30px borderless squares with the current page in a #F0F1F4 chip; no 'jump to page' input, no rows-per-page selector unless it is real.

EMPTY STATES -- one line of 13px #8A919C text inside the card ('No assets match this filter.'). No illustration, no button.

ICONS -- 16px stroke line icons at 1.5px weight, present in the sidebar, in toolbar dropdown triggers, in overflow menus and in banners; absent from table cells, form labels and definition grids.
design_tokens.spacing: 4px base unit, 8px rhythm, and only these widths exist: sidebar 264px (fixed, never resizes), content max-width 1280px then centred in the canvas, filter popover 320px, document-reader anchor list 200px, definition-grid label column 180px, table gutter column 20px, rank chip 22px. Page gutter 24px horizontal / 20px top. 20px between the page header block and the first card, 28px between stacked cards and above a new section heading, 12px between the breadcrumb and the title, 6px between the title and the grey subline, 8px between the filter-pill row and the card below it. Card padding 16px (20px for the document reader, 32px for the rendered export). Table cell padding 12px vertical inset on a 34px row, 14px horizontal; the first and last cells get 16px against the card edge so text never touches the border. Form: 8px between a label and its control, 12px between stacked fields, 16px column gap in a two-column field grid. Inline: 8px between adjacent toolbar actions, 6px between an icon and its label, 6px inside a chip, 8px between a status pill and the text beside it, 4px between a number and its unit. The authority ladder uses a 24px gap between rank cards, crossed by the connector line. Radii: 10px cards and popovers, 12px modals, 8px inputs and search fields, 6px buttons and value chips, 4px status pills, 999px removable filter pills, 2px the identity diamond. Borders are one hairline value (1px #E4E6EB on edges, #ECEEF1 on in-card row rules); the only 1.5px border in the system is a selected filter pill, and the only 3px is the active sidebar bar and the active tab underline.

structural_notes:
CHROME. There is no global top bar. A fixed 264px white left sidebar with a 1px #E4E6EB right border holds everything: at the top a scope switcher (a 44px bordered control showing the operating area with a ⌄, opening a menu of interconnect regions -- this is where the region filter lives, exactly as LaunchDarkly puts project/environment in the sidebar and Azure puts the store in the breadcrumb); beneath it a search field; then a flat 15px nav list with 20px line icons -- Overview, Setpoint Registry, Governance Policy, Commissioning Standard, Audit Readiness -- the active item a #EEF0FE fill with a 3px #4F46E5 left bar and rounded right corners; a nested group indents its children and swaps their icons for a 6px filled accent square. A collapse control and the operator's identity sit pinned at the bottom. Everything else is canvas.

PAGE HEADER, in the canvas rather than in chrome, and identical on every surface: a 12.5px grey breadcrumb line ('Setpoint Registry / North Interconnect'), then a 24px/600 title, then a 12.5px grey subline giving scope and count in plain words, then right-aligned actions on the title row -- borderless icon+label dropdown triggers first (Filters, Sort, Display) and at most one filled indigo button last. Detail pages put the record's identifier in mono directly under the title and keep the same header shape, so list and detail read as one screen with the middle swapped.

LIST → DETAIL. The registry is a single white card holding a two-line-row table: line one is the asset identifier in mono 15px/600, line two is 12.5px grey operational metadata separated by '·' (voltage class in kV, owning district, commissioning window, telemetry health as a small pill). Sorting is by an operational column by default; the identifier column is sortable but not pre-sorted. Filtering happens in a popover from the toolbar, never in a left facet column, and every applied filter also appears as a removable pill on a row beneath the header. Selecting a row NAVIGATES to the asset's configuration page -- no expanding row, no side peek. Paging is beneath the card.

DETAIL SURFACE. The asset page is a single column of white cards: an identity/definition-grid card first (nameplate rating in MVA, feeder, last inspection, maintenance notes), then the override ledger as a collapsed disclosure section whose closed state states only that a ledger exists. Expanded, it becomes a 34px-row table with columns Layer / Stored value / State, one row per layer the record actually declares, each carrying that layer's identity diamond, with the three absence conditions rendered by the sentinel component above. There is no right meta rail -- these records are too small to justify one, and the reference products do not use one on a config record.

POLICY AREA. The governance policy page is a definition grid (governing mode, identifying key field, effective date, approving committee, review cadence) plus a small card listing superseded revisions as plain rows marked 'historical'. The number of authority layers is stated as a bare integer; the layer names and their order are NOT on this page. A single secondary button opens the authority ladder as its own surface, and that ladder -- the ordered rank stack described in components -- is the only place in the product where the precedence order is drawn.

STANDARD AREA. The commissioning standard is a front-matter page (revision identity, text encoding rule) listing its three parts as titles with an 'Open' control each; the normative clause body, the conditions-of-use section and the reference annex each open as their own document-reader surface. The annex holds the one result the standard fixes by value and prints it as a mono block. Nothing on the front matter restates a clause.

AUDIT AREA. Audit readiness is a summary card (count of checks the regime is accountable for, sign-off status pill, an auditor contact definition grid) plus a primary 'Render conformance matrix' button; the individual checks exist only inside the rendered document, which opens as the paper-like export surface and can be downloaded.

OVERVIEW. The landing surface is a 3-across row of stat cards on the canvas -- frequency deviation as a large tabular-mono signed number in mHz, area load against forecast in MW with a small percentage delta, a thin stacked generation-mix bar -- above a full-width one-line advisory strip and a small alarm-count line. Two bare-integer counters ('assets under configuration management', 'conformance checks outstanding') sit as plain stat cards with a 12.5px label above a 28px mono number. No table, no identifiers.

VOCABULARY AND UNITS. Say asset, setpoint, override layer, authority rank, precedence order, resolved value, source layer, resolved / unresolved, region, interconnect, feeder, owning district, voltage class, nameplate rating, commissioning window, telemetry health, governance policy, governing mode, identifying key field, effective date, approving committee, review cadence, superseded revision, commissioning standard, normative clause, conditions of use, reference annex, conformance check, conformance matrix, sign-off. Units are written next to the number in 12.5px #5C636E -- kV, MV·A, MW, mHz, %. Counts are bare integers with no thousands separator below 10,000. Never label an unresolved asset 'error', 'missing' or 'invalid'; it is 'unresolved'. Never write 'null' in operator-facing copy -- the sentinel text is '(no value)'; 'null' appears only inside the standard's clause text, where it is a normative literal set in mono.

RESTRAINT -- the thing generated interfaces get wrong. There is no colour above the fold except one indigo button and the layer-identity diamonds. Cards have borders, not shadows; only popovers and modals have shadows. Rows never take a tinted background to convey state -- state lives in a 20px pill or an 8px glyph. There are no coloured section headers, no gradient anywhere, no icon-in-a-tinted-circle, no card with a coloured top edge, no progress ring, and no filled red or green button. Toolbars are borderless text, so the only bordered controls on a list page are the search field and the table card. Disabled means grey, not hidden.
